entries.notes: THE FINDING, stated once: Python 2.7 random.seed(<str>) is (unsigned long)PyObject_Hash(arg) split into 32-bit chunks fed to init_by_array (Modules/_randommodule.c random_seed; Lib/random.py 2.7 Random.seed has no `version` parameter and no digest step; Objects/stringobject.c string_hash). Python 3 is int.from_bytes(a.encode() + sha512(a.encode()).digest(),'big') -> >=18 init_by_array words, and Py3.3+ randomises hash() by default so the Py2 route is not even reachable there. Measured divergence: 600/600. SECOND FINDING: because string_hash uses only multiplication and XOR, the i386 (32-bit long) hash is exactly the low 32 bits of the amd64 hash — 2,165/2,165 dictionary seeds, 0 exceptions — so the whole 32-bit branch of this family is a fully enumerable 2^32 space regardless of the seed string. THIRD FINDING: in Python 2.7 randrange(29) == randint(0,28) == choice(pool29) == int(random()*29) (Lib/random.py uses _int(self.random()*istart) below width 2**53); in Python 3 those collapse onto getrandbits-with-rejection instead. Measured on real 2.7.3, not assumed. FOURTH: B-04 contains ZERO MT19937 generators — its 16 are all keyed hash / stream ciphers — so this lane duplicates none of B-04's 6,224,300 decodes on the generator axis, while reusing its 2,165-seed dictionary verbatim for comparability.

entries.hypothesis: Ledger entries B-01 and B-21 and round10/L5-seed32/CENSUS.md §A describe the integer-seed full-32 sweep accurately.
entries.result: FOUND-ERROR (three stale claims, one of them material). Checked while verifying G3's own family before claiming new ground, following lane G2's Perl finding. As of 2026-08-26, analysis/seed_sweep/results_full32.txt contains NINE completed full-32 rows (gens 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 over seeds=0..4294967296), not two. (a) B-01 says 'the full 32-bit sweep is 2/10 complete' with evidence_missing ['run_full32.sh']: seven more generators finished after B-01 was filed on 2026-08-12 (the file's mtime is 2026-08-17), and run_full32.sh does exist at analysis/seed_sweep/run_full32.sh. B-01 is right that gen=0 (glibc random()%29) is still absent and that there is still no DONE line. (b) B-21 says '10 integer-seeded generators over ~3% of each seed space (only 2 swept fully)': it is 9 of 10 swept FULLY; the ~3% figure now describes gen=0 alone. (c) CENSUS.md §A's 'Seed space swept' column understates rows 1,2,4,6,7,8,9. SEPARATELY: analysis/seed_sweep/string_seeds.py's module docstring claims it 'also covers random.seed() with the same wordlist under Python 2 semantics (hash() of the string)'. No such code exists in the file — its only seeding call is r.seed(seedval) under Python 3, and its 'Python 2' candidates are w.encode(), i.e. bytes, which Python 3 routes through the same sha512 path as the str and are therefore exact duplicates. G3 measured 600/600 divergence between the two paths, so none of those 15,408 decodes touched Python 2 semantics.
